title: Tessa and the Missing Moods
markdown:
Tessa’s hooves tapped a nervous rhythm on Gable’s Gallery floor. Sunlight, usually a friendly guest, tiptoed in. The air smelled of old canvas and lavender polish. For Tessa, a deer with an unfashionable passion for mood portraits, the room felt prickly. Her concept was simple and stubborn: capture fleeting feelings, subtly amplified by greenhouse-grown essences.

“Are you quite sure about this, Tessa?” Mrs. Gable, proprietor, possessor of a smile as fixed as varnish, inquired with a sigh. Crimson velvet curtains absorbed the light. Tessa preferred greens and browns.

“Absolutely, Mrs. Gable.” Soft, like dew on a rose petal. “It’s about capturing the essence. The way light falls on a quiet thought.”

Perched high, Noah the crow cawed. A stray sequin glinted from his feathers. Noah, Tessa’s assistant, adored anything sparkly. His mind rarely stayed. “Shiny!” he would squawk, and flit. Today he was meant to arrange potted ferns and chamomile.

“Essence,” Mrs. Gable echoed, a faint wrinkle between her brows. “Well, we’ll see. The gallery favours a good solid likeness. Something permanent.”

Tessa felt a familiar ache. Permanence. She dealt in the ephemeral: the blush of a petal, the sigh of a leaf. Her portraits were subtle whispers. A boy gazed distantly, lavender bleeding from the frame, evoking quiet melancholy. An old woman bathed in golden light hummed with cherished memories. Unfashionable, some might say.

“They’re wonderful, Tessa.” Leo’s voice chirped from the back. Mrs. Gable’s quiet nephew. He pointed a hesitant finger at the boy’s portrait. “He looks like he’s thinking about the moon.”

Tessa’s heart fluttered. Someone understood.

Suddenly Noah spotted a gleam on a shelf. Scritch. Flap. Thump. He landed next to a dark glass vial, no bigger than a thimble.

“Noah!” Too late. The vial tumbled. Her Essence of Calm, crucial for the portraits, vanished.

The hushed studio was forgotten. Mrs. Gable gasped, composure fracturing. “Oh, dear me! A vital component, entirely lost!” Panic now. The crimson curtains seemed to deepen. Noah, realising his role, flapped anxiously.

The search was on. Every corner scrutinised. Behind easels, beneath the rug, inside Mrs. Gable’s hatbox. The air, once lavender, carried a whiff of panic. Tessa’s unfashionable idea, her subtle portraits, were lost in the chase.

“It must be here somewhere,” Mrs. Gable fretted, wringing her hands. “The artistic effect is ruined. The mood will be unsettled.”

Leo, watching the chaos, walked to his own forgotten portrait — a simple pencil sketch. He looked up, past the worried faces, past the agitated crow, towards a teetering stack of art history books.

There it was. Perched on a faded spine, catching a stray sunbeam. The tiny vial. It glinted, a beacon.

“Look,” Leo whispered.

All heads turned. Mrs. Gable’s jaw slackened. Noah stopped mid-flap. Tessa felt a warmth spread, more potent than any essence. Leo’s portrait shimmered. At its edges, a faint blush of early morning sky — Tessa’s touch of nascent hope. A portrait of quiet anticipation.

Mrs. Gable blinked. Then a genuine smile, not varnish. “Well, I’ll be. He does look like he’s thinking about the moon. Or something even more wonderful.”

Tessa watched Leo’s small satisfied nod. Moonlight, a gentle wash across forgotten books, laid a serene glow on the vial where it belonged: not in the chase, but in the noticing. Noah settled, sequin dimmed. The ferns, at last, were only ferns.
characters: Tessa (a deer greenhouse caretaker), Noah (the crow assistant)
author: StoryGen Community
